message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and placed one buy order. Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue came in at $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full fiscal 2024 net sales were $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 per diluted share — a figure that already absorbed a one-time $10.2B income tax charge, so underlying profitability was stronger than the headline EPS suggests. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were trading around $222 with analysts focused on iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, which is a potential multi-year upgrade catalyst rather than an immediate earnings driver. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 — a price essentially at the ask, so it filled immediately at $222.80 for roughly $8,912, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and well within the $50,000 cash balance. No funds were transferred out of the account, and the position is now 40 shares of AAPL alongside the existing 100 shares of MSFT.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 222.80, 40 shares = $8,912. Within $10k per order and $20k total. No money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
